title: Naive cotangent comparison under strict henselization of local rings
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings (the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $B$ is the maximal ideal of $A$). Choose separable closures $k_A^{\mathrm{sep}}$, $k_B^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of their residue fields and a compatible embedding $k_A^{\mathrm{sep}}\to k_B^{\mathrm{sep}}$ extending the residue map [def-pd-separable-closure, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the strict henselizations relative to these choices [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], with the induced local homomorphism $A^{\mathrm{sh}}\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ respecting the residue embeddings. For any ring map $R\to T$, put $P=R[x_t\mid t\in T]$, $I=\ker(P\to T)$ with $x_t\mapsto t$, and $\mathrm{NL}_{T/R}=[I/I^2\xrightarrow{[h]\mapsto\mathrm dh\otimes1}\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_P T]$ in degrees $-1,0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The canonical map induced by the square of ring homomorphisms gives an isomorphism
$$\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B^{\mathrm{sh}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{NL}_{B^{\mathrm{sh}}/A^{\mathrm{sh}}}\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Mod}(B^{\mathrm{sh}}))$$
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The left side uses ordinary termwise tensor product. No Noetherian, finite-type or flatness hypothesis on $A\to B$ is required.

proof.text: Write $A_s=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $B_s=B^{\mathrm{sh}}$. By [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], $A_s$ is the colimit, as an $A$-algebra, of the forgetful diagram on the category of pairs $(S,\chi)$ with $S$ an etale $A$-algebra and $\chi:S\to k_A^{\mathrm{sep}}$ an $A$-algebra map; this is the full subcategory of etale $A$-algebras in the over-category of $k_A^{\mathrm{sep}}$, which is filtered by [lem-sc-pointed-etale-filtered] (applied to the local ring $A$ and the separable closure $k_A^{\mathrm{sep}}$). Hence $A_s$ is a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras, and in the same way, with $B$ and $k_B^{\mathrm{sep}}$, $B_s$ is a filtered colimit of etale $B$-algebras. Each stage is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization](1). This is the ind-etale condition [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. By [lem-sfb-ind-etale-naive-cotangent-acyclic], the differentials of $\mathrm{NL}_{A_s/A}$ and $\mathrm{NL}_{B_s/B}$ are isomorphisms. The first remains an isomorphism after termwise tensor with $B_s$, since a functor sends an inverse to an inverse. Thus $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{A_s/A}\otimes_{A_s}B_s)=0$, $\Omega_{A_s/A}=0$, and $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B_s/B})=\Omega_{B_s/B}=0$; the identifications of cokernels with differentials are [lem-weil-pbc-naive-cotangent-complex-cokernel-kahler].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] to $A\to A_s\to B_s$. Its first term and its fourth term vanish by step 1. Exactness therefore makes the canonical map $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B_s/A})\to H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B_s/A_s})$ both injective and surjective: its kernel is the image of the zero first term and its cokernel maps injectively into the zero fourth term. The same sequence ends in $0\to\Omega_{B_s/A}\to\Omega_{B_s/A_s}\to0$. Hence the coefficient-change chain map $v:\mathrm{NL}_{B_s/A}\to\mathrm{NL}_{B_s/A_s}$ is an isomorphism on both cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 0D08 (lemma-henselization-NL), Jacobi-Zariski for A to its strict henselization to the strict henselization of B.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] to $A\to B\to B_s$. The canonical map $u:\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B_s\to\mathrm{NL}_{B_s/A}$ is surjective on $H^{-1}$ because the following term $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B_s/B})$ is zero. It is injective on $H^{-1}$ by [lem-sfb-ind-etale-jacobi-zariski-left-injective], using the ind-etale final map proved in step 1. The same exact sequence and the two vanishings for $B_s/B$ give $\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B B_s\cong\Omega_{B_s/A}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-naive-cotangent-complex-cokernel-kahler] and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], these are precisely the degree-zero cohomology modules of the source and target of $u$, with the same induced map. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism on both cohomology groups. No replacement of $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}\otimes B_s)$ by $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL})\otimes B_s$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0D08 (lemma-henselization-NL), six-term sequence for A to B to its strict henselization.

proof.text: The composite $vu$ is the specified square-induced chain map. On polynomial presentations it sends coefficients $a$ to their images in $A_s$ and sends $x_b$ to $x_{\bar b}$, where $\bar b$ is the image of $b$ in $B_s$. On conormal elements it sends $[g]\otimes c$ to $c[g^{\sharp}]$, and on differential symbols it sends $\mathrm dx_b\otimes c$ to $c\,\mathrm dx_{\bar b}$. These are exactly the formulas obtained by composing the two maps. Both maps induce isomorphisms in degrees $-1,0$ by steps 2 and 3; all other cohomology groups are zero because the complexes have only these two terms. Hence $vu$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The localization defining $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_s))$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] inverts it and gives the asserted isomorphism.
